Two major streaming platforms, HBO Max and Paramount+, may not end up merging after all.

The plan was announced in March this year, when Netflix dropped out of the bidding for Warner Bros Discovery. However, a federal judge has now issued a temporary restraining order blocking the deal from going through — at least for now…

The Merger Plan

Under the deal, Paramount would acquire Warner Bros Discovery, with its streaming platforms HBO Max and Paramount+ combined into a single service.

The Restraining Order

Viewers have responded coolly to the plan, worried that a merger would reduce competition and push up prices. A coalition of 12 state attorneys general shared those concerns and asked a federal court to impose a temporary restraining order on the deal. The court has now granted that request, according to NBC News.

The restraining order lasts 14 days, during which a hearing will take place. Even if Paramount wins the case, the merger is already under review by the EU and UK governments. The Writers Guild of America has also filed an antitrust lawsuit, arguing the merger will lead to job cuts and lower pay.
